title: Keap Review (2026)
intro: Keap is a small-business CRM and marketing automation platform combining pipelines, campaigns, SMS, payments, and AI assistants. This review covers Max Ignite/Grow/Scale pricing, core capabilities, limitations, and when to choose alternatives.
summary: Keap fits SMBs that want automation and marketing tools bundled with CRM. Max Ignite at $249/mo annual is the entry point for two users. Scores reflect first-party research, not hands-on lab testing.
verdict: Keap is a strong SMB CRM + marketing automation suite for small businesses that need campaigns, automations, and payments together — not a cheap pipeline-only CRM. Max Ignite at $249/mo annual is the practical entry; budget additional users at $39/mo. This review is based on first-party product and pricing research — not hands-on product testing.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Keap’s SMB packaging and automation templates lower the barrier versus enterprise suites, but the product spans CRM, campaigns, SMS, and payments — more surface area than a pipeline-only CRM.
Sales pipelines and opportunity tracking are documented, yet Keap’s primary story is automation and marketing ops rather than visual pipeline-first selling.
Automation is the product’s clearest strength: campaign templates, lifecycle automation, and AI Automation Assistant are first-party documented core capabilities.
Email sync, templates, broadcasts, and AI content assistance are documented alongside SMS marketing — strong for SMB marketing email, not just sales sync.
Reporting hub and ROI-oriented reports are documented on pricing/feature pages; depth is solid for SMB operators though not the primary differentiator.
Forms, custom processes, and automation blueprints support SMB process fit; less of a highly configurable enterprise CRM canvas.
App connections plus payment processors (Keap Pay, Stripe, PayPal) and Zapier-style automation are documented; marketplace breadth is secondary to built-in automation.
Implementation packages, annual-contract terms, voice/SMS tier choices, and contact capacity planning add setup/ops burden versus lightweight CRMs.
Max Grow/Scale raise contact and channel capacity, but packaging remains SMB-tier; mid-market buyers may outgrow before enterprise CRM needs are met.
$249/mo annual entry for two users is a high floor versus Capsule/Streak; value improves when buyers need automation + payments + campaigns in one stack.

whoShouldConsiderAlternatives: Teams that want free/simple CRM, Gmail-native pipelines, or pipeline-first sales UX should compare Capsule, Streak, or Pipedrive.

faq.question: How much does Keap cost?
faq.answer: Keap’s Max Ignite starts at $249/month when billed annually ($299 monthly). Max Grow is $329/$399 and Max Scale is $499/$599 (annual/monthly). Plans include two users; additional users are $39/month. Always confirm on Keap’s pricing page.

faq.question: Does Keap have a free plan?
faq.answer: No permanent free plan is published. Keap offers a free trial so you can evaluate the product.

faq.question: Is Keap mainly a CRM or marketing automation tool?
faq.answer: Both. Keap positions as an SMB CRM with marketing automation, email/SMS, payments, and sales pipelines in one platform.

faq.question: Is this a hands-on SoftwareGlimpse lab review?
faq.answer: No. This review is approved based on first-party Keap pricing and product research. SoftwareGlimpse has not recorded hands-on product testing for Keap in this assessment.

sections.heading: What Keap is
sections.body: Keap is a small-business CRM and automation platform. It combines contact/pipeline management with marketing campaigns, SMS, scheduling, and payments rather than focusing only on sales boards.

sections.heading: Pricing and plans
sections.body: Current Max packaging is Ignite, Grow, and Scale. Annual USD list pricing starts at $249/mo for Ignite and rises with contact/channel capacity on Grow and Scale. Two users are included; add seats at $39/mo.

sections.heading: Core capabilities
sections.body: Documented strengths include automation templates, email/SMS marketing, AI assistants, CRM pipelines, payments, and mobile access. Buyers should expect a broader ops suite than a lightweight CRM.

sections.heading: Who it’s for
sections.body: Best for SMBs that want automation and marketing bundled with CRM. Less ideal for free-forever buyers or pipeline-only sales teams.

productExperience.summary: Based on Keap’s documented workflow, teams typically capture leads via forms, nurture with automations and campaigns, advance opportunities in a pipeline, take payments, and review results in reporting — with AI assistants helping create content and campaigns.

body: Keap earns a solid recommendation for SMBs that want an automation suite, not just a CRM board. The documented strengths — campaigns, AI assistants, payments, and Max packaging — align with operators who run marketing and sales from one system.

The main buying risk is overpaying for suite depth you will not use. If you only need contacts and pipelines, Capsule or Streak are usually better value. This SoftwareGlimpse review is research-based, not a hands-on lab evaluation.

deepReview.keyTakeaway: Keap is best when you need CRM plus marketing automation — budget Max Ignite or higher, not a bargain pipeline tool.
